generator_view.scenario: A parent has old Xbox 360, PlayStation 3, and Wii discs and wants an inexpensive second-hand console for two children to use together on one television. The parent cares about which surviving hardware revision is likely to be a sensible purchase, what commonly relevant console, disc-drive, controller, power, video, and motion-control problems must be checked, whether two complete controller setups and the children's couch games will work, and the real cost after missing or replacement accessories. The research set has selected console and controller seller snapshots, platform and controller background, revision-sensitive failure history for one family, and narrowly scoped community questions, but it does not contain an inspected exact unit, a matched Wii console offer, a comparable population-quality study for every exact revision, or a completed two-child trial.
generator_view.target: Help the parent compare used Xbox 360, PlayStation 3, and Wii paths for two children without pretending that a platform name, seller label, rating, or anecdote proves longevity. Explain what the available revision-sensitive history can and cannot establish, audit the exact unit and two-controller or remote setup, verify the children's actual local-multiplayer discs and required accessories, include the full current cost, and end with a reversible inspection-and-trial rule that selects only the cheapest exact configuration that passes every predeclared gate or defers.
